fundamental.method_reasoning: JPM is a deposit-funded universal bank with negative reported operating cash flow driven by balance-sheet growth and no tagged capex or FCF, so an FCF DCF is not constructible; excess return on equity (residual income) anchored on book equity, ROE and payout is the correct primary frame, cross-check

band_dissents.reasoning: Terminal book-value growth for a bank should approximate sustainable growth = ROE x retention. FY2025 retention was only ~15.5% (total payout 84.5% of net income), implying ~2.4% internally funded book growth, while observed equity growth was 5.1% including AOCI. A 2.5-4% terminal band brackets both the retention math and nominal GDP; anything above ~4% would require either a permanent cut in the ~$48B/yr capital return pace or ROE sustained above the historical 15-16%.

dcf_judgment_range.basis: ±15% band on residual-income base (not a full stress test)

wacc.reasoning: For a residual-income model the discount rate should be cost of equity, not a debt-blended WACC. A large-cap, systemically important, deposit-rich bank with 12.2x asset/equity leverage and a diversified NII/fee split (52.3%/47.7%) supports a 9-10.5% CoE: above a pure-utility rate because of markets/CIB beta and policy tail risk (Dimon's own stagflation/Fed-independence warnings), but not above 11% given the deposit franchise and 57% loan/deposit ratio. Note the engine's implied discount rate is opaque here (WACC=n/a) — if it is running a debt-inclusive WACC below ~9% the residual-income value is overstated; if above ~10.5% it under-credits the franchise.

g_high.reasoning: Near-term equity/earnings growth should sit between the depressed FY2025 print and the hot Q1 2026 run-rate. FY2025 revenue grew 2.8% and net income FELL 2.4% on a $3.5B provision build and $3.8B expense build; Q1 2026 annualizes to ~$66B net income (~18.1% ROE) but was flattered by an equities-trading-led beat that should be haircut. A 3-6% band respects both: the low end reflects an easing-cycle NII fade off a 10.1% 2019-24 rate-driven CAGR that management itself concedes is a rate artifact, the high end reflects loan growth of 10.9% and the CIB/AI-issuance fee tailwind.

fade_years.reasoning: A long fade is appropriate for JPM specifically: scale, #1 global IB wallet share (~8.9%), a 2.56T deposit base and a 57% loan/deposit ratio are durable structural advantages that should decay slowly rather than cliff. Pairing a shorter explicit excess-return window with a 5-10 year fade toward cost of equity preserves franchise credit without assuming a decade of undiminished ~16% ROE.
